claimant_lives_in_uk.description: Whether the claimant lives in the UK.

children.description: A list of children the claimant is claiming for.

lives_with_claimant.description: Whether the child lives with the claimant.

in_approved_education.description: Whether the child is in approved education or training (e.g. A-levels, GCSEs, NVQ up to level 3). Only relevant for children aged 16-19.

in_extension_period.description: Whether the child (aged 16 or 17) has left education and registered with a government-sponsored careers service or the armed forces (qualifying for a 20-week extension).

upkeep_per_week.description: The amount in £ per week the claimant contributes towards the child's upkeep (food, clothes, pocket money, etc.). Only relevant if the child does not live with the claimant.

another_claimant_has_priority.description: Whether another person who also lives with the child has priority for claiming Child Benefit.

another_claimant_lives_with_child.description: Whether someone who lives with the child is already claiming Child Benefit for them.

care_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in local authority care.

care_home_24h_per_week.description: Whether the child spends at least 24 hours per week at home while in local authority care.

hospital_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in hospital or residential accommodation.

claimant_spends_on_child.description: Whether the claimant regularly spends money on the child (e.g. food, clothes, books) while the child is in hospital or residential accommodation.

is_fostered.description: Whether the child is fostered by the claimant.

council_pays_for_child.description: Whether the local council pays towards the child's accommodation or maintenance.

works_24_plus_hours.description: Whether the child works 24 or more hours per week in paid employment.

started_apprenticeship_in_england.description: Whether the child has started an apprenticeship in England.

receives_qualifying_benefits.description: Whether the child receives qualifying benefits in their own right, such as Universal Credit or Employment and Support Allowance.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text: I'll help you determine if you're eligible for Child Benefit. Let me start by getting the first question in the assessment.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Great! Let me start by asking about the child(ren) you're claiming for.

**How old is the child you'd like to claim Child Benefit for?**

The eligibility depends on their age category:
- **Under 16**: Generally qualify automatically
- **16-19 years old**: Need to be in full-time education or approved training
- **20 or over**: Would not qualify

Please tell me the child's age, or if you have multiple children, you can provide all their ages and I'll check each one.

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Hi! I'm looking to claim Child Benefit for my son, Alex. He's 19 years old and lives at home with me.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that information! I'm assessing eligibility for your son **Alex, who is 19 years old**.

Since Alex is in the 16-19 age range, I need to check whether he meets the education or training requirements. Let me ask you:

**Is Alex currently in full-time education or approved training?**

For example, this could include:
- Full-time study at school, college, or university
- An approved apprenticeship or training scheme
- Certain government-approved training programmes

Please let me know his current status.

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, Alex is in full-time education. He's studying for his A-levels at college.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Excellent! Thank you for that information. Since Alex is 19 years old and in full-time education (studying A-levels at college), this is positive for his eligibility.

Let me navigate to the next check to continue the assessment.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Perfect! Since Alex is currently in full-time education, let me move forward with validating the type and level of education.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Great! Now I need to validate the specific details about Alex's education. Based on the criteria, I need to confirm:

**Alex is studying A-levels - is this correct?** 

A-levels are approved (non-advanced) education, which is good for Child Benefit purposes. However, I need to confirm a few more details:

1. **Is Alex studying full-time at college?** (at least 12 hours per week of supervised study)
2. **Is this course employer-funded** (i.e., paid for by an employer), or is it standard college education?
3. **Is Alex married?** (This can affect eligibility if the answer is yes)

Please confirm these details so I can proceed with the assessment.

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, that's correct - Alex is studying A-levels full-time at college. It's definitely more than 12 hours a week of study. It's just standard college education, not paid for by an employer. And no, Alex isn't married.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Perfect! Thank you for confirming those details. Alex is clearly in approved full-time education (A-levels at college, 12+ hours per week, standard education, and not married). This means he meets the education level requirements.

Now let me proceed to the next check.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Excellent! Now I need to check about Alex's work situation:

**Is Alex working less than 24 hours per week, or is he not in paid work at all?**

This is important because even though Alex is in full-time education, if he's working 24 hours or more per week, it could affect his eligibility. Part-time work up to 23 hours per week is fine.

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Actually, Alex does work quite a bit - he has a full-time job at the local supermarket alongside his studies. It's definitely 24 hours or more per week.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text: I understand - thank you for clarifying that. Unfortunately, this is a significant issue for Alex's eligibility. Let me navigate to confirm the outcome.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
I now have the outcome for Alex. Let me provide you with the eligibility decision:

---

## **Child Benefit Eligibility Decision**

**For: Alex (age 19)**

### **Result: INELIGIBLE ❌**

### **Reason:**

Even though Alex is in full-time approved education (A-levels at college), he is working 24 or more hours per week. According to Child Benefit rules, children aged 16 and over who work 24+ hours per week are not eligible for Child Benefit, regardless of their education status.

### **Important Information:**

The key rule is that **paid work of 24 hours or more per week disqualifies someone from Child Benefit eligibility** when they are in this age range. Alex's full-time supermarket job (24+ hours) is the limiting factor here.

### **Next Steps:**

If Alex's work situation changes in the future - for example, if he reduces his hours to less than 24 hours per week - you may be able to claim Child Benefit again. You would need to notify HMRC of the change in circumstances.

---

I've assessed Alex's eligibility based on the official Child Benefit specification. If you have any other children you'd like me to check, or if you'd like more information about this decision, please let me know!

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: I see. Thank you for checking that for me. Just to be clear though - even though he's still doing his A-levels full-time at college, the fact that he works more than 24 hours a week means I can't get Child Benefit for him?

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Yes, that's correct. I understand this might be frustrating, but unfortunately **the 24+ hours per week work rule overrides the full-time education status** for Child Benefit purposes.

Here's how the rules work:

**For 16-19 year olds:**
- If they're in approved full-time education (like A-levels), they can normally qualify for Child Benefit
- **However**, if they're also working 24 or more hours per week in paid work, this disqualifies them - even if they're still studying full-time

In Alex's case:
- ✅ He's in approved full-time education (A-levels)
- ✅ He's studying 12+ hours per week
- ❌ But he's working 24+ hours per week at the supermarket

The work disqualification takes precedence over the education qualification.

**The only way to regain eligibility would be if:**
- Alex reduces his work hours to **less than 24 hours per week** (so 23 hours or fewer), while continuing his full-time studies

If that were to happen, you could potentially claim Child Benefit again - you'd just need to notify HMRC of the change in circumstances.

I appreciate this isn't the outcome you were hoping for. Is there anything else I can help clarify about this decision?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Right, I understand now. That's disappointing but I appreciate you explaining it clearly. Thank you for your help.

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
You're very welcome! I'm glad I could explain the situation clearly, even though it's disappointing news. You handled the assessment really well by providing all the necessary information.

Just to recap for your records:
- **Alex is currently ineligible** for Child Benefit because he's working 24+ hours per week
- **If his circumstances change** (particularly if he reduces his work hours to under 24 hours per week), you can reapply or contact HMRC to update your claim

If you have any other questions about Child Benefit in the future, or if there are other children you'd like me to check eligibility for, feel free to ask. 

Best of luck with Alex's studies and work balance - it sounds like he's managing quite a lot juggling A-levels and a full-time job!

Take care, and thank you for using this service.

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Thank you, that's really kind of you to say. Alex is definitely keeping busy! I'll keep that in mind about the hours if things change. Have a good day!

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text: You too! All the best to you and Alex. Take care! 👋

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: You're welcome! Goodbye! 👋

conversation.author: child_benefit_eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Goodbye! 👋
